solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Critical remark made by stalwart at club

parts.note: a brick is an informal word for a reliable, stalwart person
a bat is a club used in games such as cricket

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter makes a cutting comment at the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a piece of hurled masonry, and figuratively a piece of harsh criticism.

clue.text: Bishop, most flexible, and most cheerful

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
lithe means supple, so the superlative is most flexible

explanation.surface: A bishop who is both the most supple and the happiest of clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe is a literary synonym for carefree and happy, so its superlative is the happiest.

clue.text: Wearing, fixed sign indicating hospitals

parts.note: in means wearing, as in a man in a suit
firm means fixed or secure
Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A permanent sign is put up to point the way to the hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirmaries are hospitals, especially those attached to institutions or older towns.

clue.text: Novel child tipped as a certain winner?

parts.note: kid is an informal word for a child
a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection, so a napped horse is tipped to win

explanation.surface: A youngster is tipped to come first, perhaps in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: KIDNAPPED is the Robert Louis Stevenson novel; NAP is British racing jargon for the tipster's best bet of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapped is a famous adventure story by Robert Louis Stevenson, an instance of a novel.

clue.text: Earmark a tax to be raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it upwards, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy, as on a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Money set aside for a levy that is due to go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be raised' turns A TOLL upwards in the down light, giving its letters in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot funds is to assign them for a purpose, just as earmarking does.

clue.text: Design incomplete, however

indicators.note: incomplete says the word loses its final letter, here a T

parts.note: a thought can be an intention or plan, as in a design

explanation.surface: A plan is left unfinished, though not for want of trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the last T from THOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Though used as an adverb at the end of a sentence means however or nevertheless.

clue.text: Damage around English women's quarters

indicators.note: around says the word for damage goes round the letter for English

parts.note: to harm is to damage

explanation.surface: Vandals wreck the area round the English ladies' rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the separate part of a Muslim household reserved for wives and female relatives.

clue.text: Employ trick to get rid of head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter, here R

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: Hire a con artist to remove the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get rid of head' drops the R from RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to employ it, the two verbs being synonyms.

clue.text: Snag affected church

parts.note: hit means affected, as a town hit by floods

explanation.surface: A problem had an impact on the parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like an anagram signal for church, but CHURCH has six letters; it is HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a temporary difficulty or snag that holds things up.

clue.text: His read out — name dramatist

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the preceding words are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud a famous playwright's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' looks like reading aloud, but 'out' is the anagram signal. Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an Irish-born playwright of eighteenth-century comedies of manners.

clue.text: Disbeliever, elected female, lied atrociously

parts.note: in means elected, as a party that is in power

indicators.note: atrociously says the letters are treated badly, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A sceptic who was voted in, a woman, told dreadful lies.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is one who rejects a particular religious faith, an unbeliever.

clue.text: Right book put in there, novel for a metaphysical poet

indicators.note: put in says the two abbreviations go inside the following word
novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book is placed on the shelf there, a novel for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets R and B inside THERE, and 'novel' then rearranges all seven letters. George Herbert was a seventeenth-century Metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: George Herbert, author of The Temple, is one of the English Metaphysical poets alongside Donne.

clue.text: Hence, three fare badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are jumbled up rather than kept in order

explanation.surface: So three people do poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence can mean from this time on, which is the adverbial sense of hereafter.

clue.text: Norwegian painter, one leaving German city

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for one goes away from the city name

parts.note: Munich is the capital of Bavaria in Germany
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian artist departs from a Bavarian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Munch, painter of The Scream, was Norway's most famous artist.

clue.text: Serenade Ivy, desperately — don't give up

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A suitor sings frantically to a woman called Ivy, refusing to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Never say die is an idiom urging someone to keep going and not admit defeat.

clue.text: Note coming from small musical instrument

parts.note: a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A musical sound comes out of a little instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp is a note raised by a semitone, written with the hash-like sign.

clue.text: Tranquilliser used in extremely severe case

indicators.note: extremely picks the extremes, the outermost letters, of the next word

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case, used for indirect objects

explanation.surface: A calming drug is given in a very serious medical case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a patient, but it is a grammatical case: SE from the ends of 'severe', then DATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a drug that calms or tranquillises.

clue.text: One rowing close to pantry in part of kitchen

parts.note: a sculler is a rower who uses a pair of sculls

indicators.note: close to means the end of the next word, its last letter

explanation.surface: An oarsman stands near the larder in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is a back room off the kitchen used for washing dishes and other rough work.

clue.text: Here today gone tomorrow in ten trains abroad

indicators.note: abroad means wandering far away, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Ten foreign trains appear and quickly vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient lasts only briefly, which the phrase about today and tomorrow describes.

clue.text: Filbert produced by head girl at the start

indicators.note: at the start says the girl's name comes first, before the word for head

parts.note: Hazel is a girl's name
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A head girl is responsible for a kind of nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head girl' looks like a school prefect, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'at the start' puts the girl before the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is the cultivated hazel tree's nut, another name for a cobnut or hazelnut.

clue.text: Complaint coming from wife and trendy daughter by small stream

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a brook

explanation.surface: A wife and her stylish daughter grumble about a little brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Windburn is a skin condition, and complaint can mean a minor ailment.

clue.text: Vessel from Tampa or Tacoma

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A ship sails from one American port or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship sailing from Tampa or Tacoma; it is a blood vessel, picked out of 'Tampa or'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, and a blood vessel.

clue.text: Society member, mother, and child

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A family of mother and child join a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mason, or Freemason, belongs to the fraternal Society of Freemasons.

clue.text: Dark brown coffee, second, man's not finished

parts.note: mo is short for moment, so a second

indicators.note: not finished says the word loses its final letter, here a P

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man

explanation.surface: A man has not quite finished his coffee in a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coffee' sits between definition and wordplay but mocha is also a coffee; 'not finished' drops the P from CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a dark brown colour named after the coffee shipped from the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Hotel in French resort aimed at a small specialised market

definitions.text: aimed at a small specialised market

indicators.note: in places the letter for hotel inside the resort's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
Hotel is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: A hotel on the Riviera is targeted at a narrow clientele.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche product or business serves a small specialised segment of buyers.

clue.text: Comes down on head causing a scene

parts.note: lands means touches down, as an aircraft does
a cape or headland is a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone falls on their head, causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing a scene' reads as an idiom for a fuss; 'scene' is the definition, a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a view of the countryside, or a painting of one, a scene.

clue.text: Egg on sappers to bring out saltpetre

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British army's sappers

explanation.surface: Urging on army engineers to produce an explosive ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as urge; 'Egg' is NIT, put on RE in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is an old name for potassium nitrate, otherwise called saltpetre.

clue.text: Opportunist in court, briefly

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter Y

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court

explanation.surface: A chancer is caught out in court after a short hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is British slang for someone who takes risky opportunities for personal gain.

clue.text: See 27
Adore art in resort — it makes one feel exhilarated

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means to sort again, putting the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Loving the art on show at a holiday town gives a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in resort' reads as a holiday place, but 'in' is fodder and 'resort' means sort again, rearranging ADORE ART IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread on air is an idiom for feeling elated, as if walking without touching the ground.

clue.text: A deadly sin, granted

parts.note: greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Avarice is conceded to be one of the worst sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Granted and agreed both mean conceded or allowed, as in an agreed point.

clue.text: Purchase not fashionable, a robe

indicators.note: not says the following word's letters are taken away from the first

parts.note: an investment is a purchase made in the hope of a return
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An unfashionable gown is bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe, especially one worn by clergy.
